component.name: trebaruna
component.summary: Sign and check documents with the European signature formats
Firma y comprueba documentos con los formatos de firma europeos
Signa i comprova documents amb els formats de signatura europeus
Asina e comproba documentos cos formatos de sinatura europeos
Sinatu eta egiaztatu dokumentuak Europako sinadura-formatuekin
Firma e verifica documenti con i formati di firma europei

description.p: trebaruna signs PDF, XML and any other file with a certificate on a file, a smart card, Firefox or a remote signing service, and checks signatures against the European trust lists. It replaces AutoFirma, and answers the afirma:// requests of public administration websites.

ul.li: PAdES, CAdES, XAdES, XMLDSig, ASiC, OpenDocument and Office Open XML signatures
Timestamps, long-term validation and archival levels
A visible seal you place on the page, with an optional handwritten signature
Every network connection it makes is listed in the result

description.p: Signatures added to a CAdES envelope at LT carry their timestamp authority's validation data.
Long-term signatures carry their timestamp authority's validation data, as the European Commission's validator expects.
CAdES long-term signatures carry their revocation answers as other validators read them.
CAdES archive timestamps are accepted by the European Commission's validator.
Cards with Brainpool keys, such as German health professionals' cards, sign.
The PDF form fields a signature locks become read-only.
PDF form fields that set requirements for their signature are honoured.
PDF form fields that lock others when signed are honoured.
A PDF certified against any change is never signed.
Counter-signing a timestamped XML signature keeps its timestamp.
Every archive timestamp of an XML signature is checked, and each signature by its own timestamps.
ASiC containers can be counter-signed, from the command line, the window and web pages.
Detached XML signatures can be counter-signed.
The certificate command speaks one language, the reader's.
ASiC containers open in Java's ZIP reader; added entries are dated.
Co-signed containers report the kind of signature added; documents declare their real media type.
Counter-signatures and co-signatures inside containers keep names of their own.
A detached signature checked without its document is reported as unknown.
Clearer verification output: field names, the reason, one time zone.
Signing no longer replaces an earlier signed file without saying so.
Failures are JSON too when JSON is asked for.
Trusted lists' brainpool authorities anchor signatures like any other.
XML signatures made with brainpool keys are read and checked.
Names, reasons and places with accents read correctly in signatures with a seal.
PDF signatures made with brainpool keys are checked, no longer reported as changed.
CAdES signatures made with brainpool keys, as German health professionals' cards make them, are read and checked.
PDF/A documents stay PDF/A when you sign them with a seal.
The window asks for the password of a protected PDF.
Sign PDFs protected with a password, keeping them encrypted.
An address book of the people you encrypt for, in the command line and the envelopes window.
Change a card's PUK, from the command line or the Card menu.
The window makes ASiC containers, signs FacturaE invoices as such and declares signature policies.
When a page asks for a visible signature, you place the seal on its PDF in the approval window.
XML signatures over documents a page names by address and digest (Externally Detached, manifests), every one listed before you approve.
In a session with a page, the certificate it asked to keep is offered again, ticked; you still approve every request.
ASiC-S containers made through the site's server (CAdES-ASiC-S-tri, XAdES-ASiC-S-tri).
Pages that name FacturaEtri, Adobe PDF TriPhase or PKCS1 are understood.
Pages that send a document's digest instead of the document get a CAdES signature over it, with the digest shown before you approve.
Pages that ask for a bare signature of a few bytes (NONE) get it, with the approval saying what such a signature does and does not record.
Pages that ask for the signing certificate of the identity card you logged in with find it.
Administration pages that talk to AutoFirma over its local WebSocket channel work, once the local certificate is installed.
The certificate for the local channel AutoFirma pages use, opt-in.
Clearer messages for a missing document or passphrase.
Approving a signature prepared by a site's server names that server.
Content hidden in an element that only looks like an XML signature is reported as unsigned.
Only a token that declares itself a timestamp is read as one.
The EU list of the lists is authenticated against the keys the Official Journal announced.
PDF timestamps are judged against the trust lists, and one from an unknown authority still counts as a timestamp.
The visible seal's text is drawn with the right letter spacing and characters.
Web pages that speak AutoFirma's protocol can have an ASiC container co-signed.
A PDF whose signature envelope carries other content is left to the PDF library's verdict.
PDF timestamps from authorities that sign with RSA-PSS are checked against the document.
The window signs with a key kept by a remote signing service.
Remote signatures can be authorised in the browser, through the provider's OAuth2 server.
A remote signature asks the provider for the credential once.
The window encrypts documents for others and opens encrypted envelopes.
The Flatpak signs with smart cards.
The window follows the desktop's light or dark preference.
Timestamps an authority signed with RSA-PSS are read as valid.
ASiC containers are co-signed.
ASiC time-stamped containers are made and verified.
XML signatures declare where they were made, and web page approvals show the policy, roles and place a signature will declare.
Verification shows the policy, the roles and the place a signature declares.
Web pages sign single documents through the site's server (the …tri formats).
XAdES signatures are counter-signed inside the document, from the command line and from web pages.
Signatures added to a CAdES envelope take levels LT and LTA.
CAdES-LTA archive timestamps follow EN 319 122-1 and are checked by verification.
The window and web pages sign a PDF form in its signature field; trebaruna fields lists a form's empty fields.
PDF signatures declare a signature policy, such as the AGE's, from the command line and from web pages.
A PAdES B-LT signature added to a signed PDF keys its revocation entry to itself.
A PDF form is signed in its empty signature field, the seal drawn in the field's box.
The seal is laid out apart from the PDF library that draws it.
CMS and PDF signatures made with RSA-PSS are verified, and chains reach German authorities with RSA-PSS keys.
Trusted lists download from servers that refuse unnamed clients, and the EU list is read once per sync.
XML signatures made with RSA-PSS or SHA-3 are verified; the German trusted list authenticates.
A trusted list is used only when its own signature signs the whole list.
Verification names the parts of an XML document a signature leaves out.
Verification checks the XAdES archive timestamp imprint.
Verification checks the signing-certificate binding.
Accessibility: contrast, keyboard resizing of the seal, names for screen readers.
The page preview works without poppler.
Packages: .deb, Flatpak, AppImage and a Windows installer.
